desc: Name the missing primitive. In copy_highpage, immediately before copy_page(), try ONE change per build and run scripts/t6040-cow-repro.sh 4x at maxcpus=2 after each: (a) smp_mb() only; (b) a single volatile read of kto only; (c) a single volatile read of kfrom only; (d) flush_dcache_page(to) / __flush_dcache_area equivalent on the destination; (e) nothing (control, = 208). The cheapest variant that makes the fault vanish names what the CoW path is missing on this hardware. If (a) suffices it is an ordering bug; if only (d) suffices it is cache maintenance; if only the full virt_addr_valid() work suffices it is a timing artefact and the real bug is elsewhere. Depends on 208 passing. This is the ticket most likely to produce an upstreamable patch. UNBLOCKED 2026-08-03: 208 passed, so the suppression is real. Follow 208s method rule: fresh-boot baseline + >=4 runs per variant, run 1 is the sensitive one. RESULT 2026-08-03: (a) smp_mb() only -> 0 traces/4 runs (clean); (b) volatile READ of kto with NO barrier -> ALSO 0 traces/4 runs; (e) control un-instrumented -> 2 traces. So ANY small perturbation before copy_page suppresses the fault and (a) proved nothing about ordering. MISSING-BARRIER HYPOTHESIS REFUTED. The bug is a timing-sensitive race NOT located in copy_highpage -- copy_page is where the fault is TAKEN, not where the bug lives. Do NOT ship (a) or (b) as a fix. New direction: a kernel-mode fault on a LINEAR-MAP address with valid aligned args means the mapping changed under us => page lifetime/refcount or TLBI-completion bug, not ordering. Highest-value next action is now an upstream report with scripts/t6040-cow-repro.sh (we run untested M4 support; may be a known erratum), ahead of further local experiments.
